title: Onramp config variant compiler scratchpad
body:
Notes to self / brain dump: Onramp Config Variant Compiler (prototype)

Goal: take customer-facing compact 'onramp' config and compile it into one or more runtime-ready adapter variants arranged for hosted/dedicated/private deploys. Compiler should be able to:
- validate semantics (SLOs, quota bounds, region constraints)
- normalize/shrink config (canonicalize synonyms)
- expand high-level shorthands into concrete route/model/runtime profiles
- generate variant artifacts (json + small wasm hooks) for runtime to consume
- include deterministic fingerprint for cache keys and diffs

Why: we want one concise surface for customers but different runtime variants depending on capacity, latency tier, and model quantization availability. Also need to support canary vs stable, A/B routing, and automatic fallback variants.

High-level pass pipeline (sketch):
1) parse -> AST (preserve comments/notes for traceability)
2) static validation pass (schema + domain rules)
3) normalization pass (aliases -> canonical keys)
4) constraint solve / enrichment (fill defaults from product catalog)
5) variant expansion (cartesian-ish expansion with pruning)
6) cost/latency estimation pass (score variants)
7) policy injector (SLO -> runtime policy blocks)
8) emitter: artifact packaging + fingerprint

Example compact DSL snippet (customer-facing, YAML-like):

onramps:
  - name: mobile-chat
    route: "/v1/infer/chat"
    models:
      - family: redwood-2
        profile: fast
    latency_slo_ms: 200
    regional_pref: [us-west, us-east]
    batching:
      target_tokens: 512
      max_wait_ms: 30
    fallback: {type: model-variant, policy: degrade-latency}

Compiler expansion idea -> produces 2 variants:
- mobile-chat:hosted:fast -> model=redwood-2-ggml-q4, batching profile X, placement us-west primary
- mobile-chat:dedicated:fast -> model=redwood-2-8bit, batching profile Y, reserved pool binding

Important expansion rules (brainstorm):
- If customer specifies "profile: fast", prefer lower-latency quant variants if available; otherwise choose full-fp with GPU and set batching low.
- regional_pref list creates route-level region affinity but compiler must attach sticky fallback region ordering.
- if latency_slo < 100ms, disallow horizon/fallback that implies cold starts > 300ms (validation error)
- fallback.degrade-latency means allow higher-cost model variants with lower quality but keep latency bound — needs more precise defn

Artifact shape (flat JSON fields only; runtime expects small atlas per variant):
- id (string)
- route (string)
- model_handle (string)
- deploy_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
- batching_profile (string)
- region_affinity (list of strings)
- slo_latency_ms (number)
- fingerprint (string)
- constraints (list of strings)
- hooks (list of urls or base64 wasm blobs)

Compiler implementation notes:
- Keep passes pure/functional where possible to allow incremental compile and caching
- Use content-addressed fingerprinting: H = sha256(sorted(key-values))
- Cache granularity: per-onramp + per-variant
- Cache invalidation: linked to product-catalog version + model-availability manifest

Performance targets:
- cold compile time (first input): < 300ms for simple onramp (1 route, 2 models)
- incremental compile (change batching): < 30ms using cached pass outputs
- disk budget: artifacts should be small (<4KB each) except wasm hooks

Telemetry / observability:
- emit compile_duration_ms, variant_count, prune_ratio, validation_warnings
- attach compile fingerprint to rollout events so console can show diffs

Edge cases & unresolved questions:
- Q: How to represent cross-route constraints (shared tokens / tenant quotas)? Single onramp may define multiple routes that share a quota. Compiler needs to detect and emit shared quota bindings.
- Q: Canary rollouts: generate variant plus "guardrail" wrapper that monitors quality metrics (eval hooks) and can pause traffic. Compiler should emit a small policy stub.
- Q: Merge semantics when customer supplies multiple onramp definitions for same route in a single file: last-wins? explicit merge key? For now prefer explicit merge by name; throw if duplicate names unless explicit_merge: true.
- Q: How to express A/B split percentages at compile time vs runtime? Compiler should produce both variants and a runtime routing plan (weights) that can be adjusted without recompilation.

TODO (short):
- [ ] write canonical schema (JSON Schema + examples)
- [ ] implement normalization (alias table)
- [ ] build small local CLI that prints artifact preview
- [ ] add unit tests for latency SLO corner cases
- [ ] prototype fingerprint cache and measure incremental times

Quick notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: expansion should avoid exponential explosion. Use pruning heuristics: prefer model variants that match the profile closely; only expand to fallback variants when requested or when SLO impossible.
- Keep runtime artifact payload tiny. Push complex logic to runtime policy code (WASM) if needed rather than embedding huge decision trees in JSON.

Related links and tickets (copied):
- PR wip: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321 (compiler scaffolding)
- Jira: INF-2387 (onramp compiler requirements)
- Slack thread: #runtime-onramp (search: "variant compiler")

Sketch: ASCII diagram

[customer-config.yaml] --> [parser] --> [AST] --> [normalize] --> [enrich from product-catalog] --> [variant-expander] --> [score/prune] --> [emitter]
                                                               |                                              |
                                                               v                                              v
                                                          [policy stubs]                                [artifacts -> runtime]

Last thought: make compiler idempotent and easy to inspect (human-readable artifact dump + backrefs to source lines). Keep this file as the working notebook; will split into a proper spec once core choices are stable.
